_comment: Seeded searches: one per role_track, so a Builder who does not yet know
what role they want is shown a catalogue instead of a blank input.
tranche_four/25-search-queries.md: 'Search is the refinement tool, not the
entry point. A blank input is the wrong first experience for this
population.'
THE VOCABULARY IS extract.ROLE_TRACK, NOT A LIST INVENTED HERE. All nine
values appear exactly once and tests/test_search_queries.py asserts the
set equality against extract.py:305-308 -- adding a tenth track without
seeding it fails the suite rather than producing a track nobody can find.
WHY THE TEXT IS NOT THE TRACK NAME. A track is a machine value
('solutions_and_implementation'); a query is what someone types into
Google Jobs. Seeding the identifier verbatim would produce a provider call
for a string no employer has ever written. Each `text` below is the
ordinary-English role family the track names, in the phrasing a job board
actually uses.
WHY NOT ONE SEED PER ARCHETYPE TOO. extract.ARCHETYPE has 26 values. 26
seeded queries re-run daily is ~9% of the ~280 renewable searches/day
against a browse surface nobody has asked for; role_track exists precisely
because it is the coarser, browsable axis (schema.py's role_track block).
Nine is the catalogue.
REJECTED: adding 'entry level' or 'junior' to every seed. It is true of
the cohort and it is the wrong place to say so -- seniority is a scoring
and relevance concern (config/pursuit-criteria.json), applied to every
posting from every source. Putting it in the query text would narrow the
provider call to postings whose TITLE says junior, which is a small and
unrepresentative slice, and it would do it invisibly.
REJECTED: a per-seed location. Every seed uses the cohort's city, which
is searchnorm.DEFAULT_LOCATION. A remote-only seed was considered and
dropped: remoteness is a filter on results (jobs.location_is_remote,
job_facts.remote_policy), not a different search.
_location_comment: Applied to every seed below. Left as one value rather than repeated nine
times so that changing the cohort's city is one edit, and so no seed can
_source_comment: 'track' rather than 'seeded'. searchnorm.SOURCES carries both because they
are different provenance: 'track' means 'this row exists because
role_track has this value', which is what makes the completeness test
above possible. 'seeded' is reserved for a hand-added query that is not a
track -- there are none today, and the value exists so that adding one
later does not require widening a CHECK constraint under load.

queries._comment: 'implementation' rather than 'solutions': 'solutions' alone is the single most diluted word on a job board and returns consulting, sales and IT services in roughly equal measure.

business_systems appears in BOTH extract.ARCHETYPE and extract.ROLE_TRACK at different grains, which extract.py:300-304 says is intended. The seed is the TRACK reading -- the browsable family, not the Salesforce/Workday configuration role.
